research.title: Exercise form does not always reveal target-muscle recruitment.
research.lead: The first design question was not how to display EMG. It was which signal could show whether the intended muscle was actually active during an exercise.
steps: Candidate A · physiological activity through surface EMG
Candidate B · angular displacement through visible contraction
Decision · select EMG after subtle contraction proved unreliable to observe geometrically
research.reverseCopy: 3-second individual calibration → filtering → squared signal → Kalman filtering → four relative-intensity bands → sample counts → session percentages.
research.note: The current result is a distribution of recorded time across relative EMG bands—not force, and not yet an automated coaching recommendation.

margin.lead: The survey data arrived as rows of repeated, comma-separated ethical-principle labels. Before testing a statistical question, the labels needed a stable shared coordinate space.
steps: Read CSV and preserve metadata columns
Split and count principle labels with Counter
Normalize each count by the row total
Write ordered principle dimensions and a JSON-encoded vector
Continue analysis in Google Sheets and R
margin.reverseTitle: No detected relationship is still a result.
margin.reverseCopy: The current linear models did not find a relationship between principle frequency and agreement for the principles examined. The broader similarity–relevance question remains open.
margin.note: Do not turn an ongoing question into a confident conclusion just because a portfolio page prefers closure.

diagram.title: Four objectives, no single winner.
diagram.lead: Automation, efficiency, fairness, and preference satisfaction were compared separately. The algorithm had to move from ranked preferences to a fractional allocation, then to an assignment that could actually be issued.
diagram.reverseCopy: Version 1 distributed remaining probability through random course choices. Version 2 balanced remaining course capacity against remaining student capacity to reduce unnecessary low-preference allocation.
diagram.note: Reported presentation result: about 70% top-two and 92% top-three under probabilistic assignment with maximum-weight realization. Preserve this as a reported simulation result until the original output is rerun.
